summary: Describes how to connect pseudowires across packet network domains or control plane domains, which may be in different autonomous systems or use different protocols.

eli5.summary: A pseudowire is a tunnel. This connects several tunnels end to end, like a relay, so one service can cross different networks.

how does vccv work on multi-segment pseudowires
subtitle: How to chain several pseudowires end to end, so one emulated service can cross different networks and signaling protocols.

tldr.problem: A single pseudowire needs its two end routers to reach and signal each other directly. That is not always possible or wanted, for example when the ends sit in different provider networks or when the two sides use different signaling protocols.
tldr.mechanism: A multi-segment pseudowire is built from two or more pseudowire segments joined at switching PEs. Each switching PE passes setup messages along, swaps the pseudowire label, and leaves the payload untouched.
tldr.outcome: Providers can confine control channels and key administration to the switching points, and MPLS/LDP and L2TPv3 segments can be mixed. The RFC also defines the SP-PE TLV, VCCV path checks and fault-status handling for such paths. It has since been updated by RFC 6723 and RFC 7267.

sections.title: Why Segment a Pseudowire
sections.content:
A pseudowire (PW) carries the essential elements of an emulated service, such as Frame Relay, ATM or Ethernet, from one provider edge (PE) router to another across a packet switched network (PSN). The usual form is a single-segment pseudowire (SS-PW), set up directly between two terminating PEs. Setting one up needs at least knowledge of, and reachability to, the remote PE's IP address.

The RFC names two general cases where that does not work well. In the first, the terminating PEs cannot or should not have a control channel between them. Its examples are an inter-AS setup where all control traffic between two provider networks is cryptographically signed (a multi-segment pseudowire, MS-PW, lets the providers confine key administration to the switching points), a path computed by an external entity that passes through a third PE, and hierarchical IP/MPLS networks where access networks reach the backbone. The RFC adds that PW switching does not reduce the amount of PW state each access-network PE holds.

In the second case, the signaling protocol and encapsulation differ on each segment, so an SS-PW is impossible and an MS-PW with interworking at the switching points is needed.

Segments are not independent: the PW service is instantiated across the whole MS-PW, so no segment can be signaled or be operational without the complete MS-PW being signaled at once.
sections.eli5: Sometimes the two ends of a pipe cannot talk to each other directly, or speak different languages. So you join shorter pipes, and each joint passes messages on.

sections.title: Terminating and Switching PEs
sections.content:
The RFC defines a few roles. A T-PE (terminating PE) is where the customer-facing attachment circuits are bound to a PW; one is present in the first and last segments of an MS-PW. An S-PE (switching PE) switches the control and data planes of the preceding and succeeding segments. It terminates the PSN tunnels of both, and is never the S-PE and the T-PE for the same MS-PW. The set of S-PEs traversed is the MS-PW path.

The RFC describes two ways to switch between PW domains. In the first, two separate control plane domains end on different PEs and the two PWs are stitched together using a native-service attachment circuit. In the second, the MS-PW model, one S-PE runs two control planes, one toward each T-PE, and connects PW Segment 1 to PW Segment 3. The two segments MUST be of the same PW type, but the two PSN tunnels need not use the same technology. When they are the same technology the PDU is not modified and is switched at the PW label level. When they differ, the PEs must adapt the encapsulation.

Setup runs from the T-PEs. The S-PE is first configured to connect a segment from one peer to a segment toward another, and exchanges nothing until the T-PE sends setup messages, which the S-PE immediately uses to form the setup messages for the next segment. A PW can pass through many S-PEs, and the edge PEs need no specific knowledge of how many. Routing and path selection, and converting one PW type to another at the S-PE, are out of scope.

On performance, the RFC notes that an MS-PW is no better than its worst-performing segment.
sections.eli5: The two ends of the long pipe are the endpoints, and each joint in the middle is a switch. The switch connects the left pipe to the right pipe and passes the contents along unchanged.

sections.title: Switching MPLS Pseudowires
sections.content:
When both segments are MPLS, the data plane is simple: PDUs are switched between the pseudowires at the PW label level, using a standard MPLS label swap. When pushing a new PSN label the TTL SHOULD be set to 255 or another locally configured fixed value. The only limit on the number of S-PEs is the TTL field of the PW MPLS label.

How the S-PE behaves depends on the control planes on each side. With two static control planes, the S-PE is configured to direct packets from one PW into the other and no control protocol is involved. A static PW next to a dynamic LDP PW is treated like an attachment circuit, and the S-PE acts much like a T-PE in an active signaling role. With two LDP control planes of the same FEC type, the S-PE SHOULD start passive: it does not advertise its LDP PW mapping until it has received at least one of the two from a remote PE. An MS-PW is declared UP only when all constituent SS-PWs are UP.

Each SS-PW of an MS-PW may have a different PWid, and with the generalized FEC the AGI, SAI and TAI may differ as well. When the path is not statically configured and FEC 129 is used, one T-PE SHOULD take the active role. By default the T-PE whose SAII is larger, compared as unsigned integers, becomes active, unless manual provisioning overrides this. Between FEC 128 and FEC 129 segments, the S-PE stays passive until a message arrives, then forms the matching message in the other FEC. PWids must be mapped to AGI/TAI/SAI by local configuration or other means outside the RFC.

A switching point SHOULD check the SP-PE TLV (described next) for its own IP address. If it finds it, it SHOULD break the loop and send a label release with the error code 0x0000003A, PW Loop Detected.
sections.eli5: When both pipes are the same kind, the switch just relabels the package and sends it on. Who speaks first is decided by a simple rule so the two ends do not shout at once.

sections.title: The SP-PE TLV
sections.content:
For troubleshooting, it helps to record which switching points a PW passes through. That is the job of the PW Switching Point PE TLV (SP-PE TLV), carried in the LDP message. Sending it is OPTIONAL, but a PE or S-PE MUST process it on receipt. The U bit MUST be set, for backward compatibility with T-PEs that do not support these extensions. The TLV may appear once per switching point, cannot be of length zero, is appended to the PW FEC at each S-PE, and the order of SP-PE TLVs MUST be preserved. The TLV type is 0x096D.

Inside the TLV are sub-TLVs: the PWid of the last segment (FEC 128 only), an optional description string of up to 80 characters in UTF-8, the optional local IP address of the switching point, the optional remote IP address of the last switching point or T-PE, the FEC element of the last segment (FEC 129 only), and the recommended L2 PW address format.

Interface parameters are used only at the endpoints and MUST pass unchanged across the S-PE, with a few exceptions: the optional interface description may be modified or removed, the fragmentation indicator may be inserted if the S-PE can reassemble, and the VCCV parameter must be reset to reflect what the S-PE supports. The Group ID has local significance only and MUST be mapped to a unique value allocated by the S-PE.

An S-PE may filter out all SP-PE TLVs for local policy reasons, so that upstream it looks like the T-PE. The cost is that VCCV will then work only as far as that S-PE, and the loop detection above will fail.
sections.eli5: Each joint can sign a guest book as the package passes through. Later, anyone can read the guest book to see which joints it went through, though a joint is allowed to skip signing.

sections.title: Mixing MPLS and L2TPv3 Segments
sections.content:
The RFC also covers an S-PE that has an MPLS PW on one side and an L2TPv3 PW on the other. Each may be static or dynamic, which gives four combinations. With two static ones, the S-PE is configured with which MPLS PW label maps to which L2TPv3 Session ID (and Cookie, if present), and which MPLS tunnel label maps to which destination IP address. When one side is dynamic, the static side is treated like an attachment circuit.

Between two dynamic PWs the S-PE always starts passive. An L2TPv3 PW is bidirectional and set up by a three-message exchange (ICRQ, ICRP, ICCN), while an MPLS PW is two unidirectional LSPs bonded by FEC identifiers. The identifying AVPs of an ICRQ are mapped to FEC identifiers in an LDP Label Mapping message, and the reverse. Teardown maps the L2TPv3 CDN message to an LDP Label Withdraw. Status changes signaled in L2TPv3 by an SLI message correspond to LDP Label Withdraw or the PW Status Notification.

Several LDP interface parameters MUST be mapped to L2TPv3 AVPs: Interface MTU, the maximum number of concatenated ATM cells, the PW Type, the PWid (to the Remote End ID AVP) and the generalized FEC SAI/TAI. Other parameters are unsupported across such a switch. The SP-PE TLV travels in a single L2TP AVP, Attribute Type 101, which MUST NOT be marked Mandatory.

For the data plane, packets are sent whole from one PW to the other, replacing the MPLS label stack with the L2TPv3 and IP header or the reverse. Where a shim header such as the MPLS Control Word is needed, sequence numbers have different semantics in L2TPv3, so they cannot simply be carried through. They MAY be supported by checking and regenerating them at the switch. If that is not supported and a T-PE requests sequencing, the S-PE SHOULD refuse the session with a CDN Result Code of 31, Sequencing not supported.
sections.eli5: Sometimes one pipe is a different brand from the next. The joint translates the setup words from one brand to the other so the long pipe still works.

sections.title: Checking the Path with VCCV
sections.content:
Operations, Administration and Maintenance (OAM) for MS-PWs reuses VCCV (Virtual Circuit Connectivity Verification) and the PW label TTL. The S-PE decrements the TTL of the PW label as it swaps it. When the TTL reaches 0 the packet goes to the control plane, so the sender can choose exactly which S-PE answers. VCCV capabilities are signaled in the VCCV interface parameter, and each S-PE removes the control channel types it does not support. Type 2 (MPLS Router Alert Label) is not supported for MS-PWs and MUST be removed. Types 1 and 3 can be used, and when the control word is enabled on user packets, Type 1 MUST be used.

The RFC specifies four operations: end-to-end connectivity verification, partial verification of any contiguous subset of segments, path verification (checking the SP-PE TLV path against the actual one, one S-PE at a time, OPTIONAL), and path trace (using FECs returned in the echo reply, usable on static MS-PWs, OPTIONAL). A node that is an S-PE replies to an echo request with return code 8, and the egress T-PE replies with return code 3. A trace stops immediately if no reply or an error code comes back.

VCCV is specific to the MPLS data plane. When a segment is L2TPv3, MPLS PW OAM MUST be terminated at the S-PE, which MUST NOT send the VCCV parameter.
sections.eli5: To check the long pipe, you send a test ball and say how many joints it may pass. The joint where the count runs out answers back, so you learn how far the pipe works.

sections.title: Passing Fault Status Along
sections.content:
When a PW segment has a fault, the status must reach the T-PEs. Remote status is forwarded unchanged by the S-PE. When the S-PE detects a local fault it sends an LDP notification with the PW status TLV, optionally with one SP-PE TLV, in both directions. The T-PE reads the SP-PE TLV to see where the fault occurred. With no SP-PE TLV, the status came from the remote T-PE.

Because an S-PE has no attachment circuits, only two status values apply: 0x00000008 (Local PSN-facing PW (ingress) Receive Fault) and 0x00000010 (Local PSN-facing PW (egress) Transmit Fault). A transmit fault on one segment is reported toward that side as 0x00000010 and toward the other side as 0x00000008, and a receive fault is reported the opposite way. Each S-PE stores two 32-bit status words per segment, one for local and one for remote failures, ORing in new failures.

Local faults always take priority: a remote clearing message is forwarded only if no matching local fault exists. For crossing administrative boundaries, an OPTIONAL dampening scheme similar to BGP route dampening may limit status churn, with details left to implementations.
sections.eli5: If one joint springs a leak, it tells both neighbors right away, so each end knows the pipe is broken and roughly where.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC splits security into the data plane and the control plane. For the data plane, the considerations in RFC 4447, RFC 3931 and RFC 3985 apply without change. For VCCV Type 3 with no control word, a packet with a TTL larger than the hop count, or one mishandled by an S-PE, could be forwarded out of the attachment circuit as if it were native traffic. The CE would most likely treat it as an error packet, but enabling the control word guarantees that a VCCV packet is never forwarded to the AC.

For the control plane, an incoming session request MUST NOT be accepted unless its IP source address is known to be that of an eligible peer. The set of peers may be pre-configured or learned through a trusted auto-discovery protocol, and source address spoofing must be prevented. For stronger protection the LDP authentication option or the L2TPv3 Control Message Authentication option MAY be used. Both rely on pre-shared keys, which the RFC says should be manageable for MS-PWs because few links leave an organization.
sections.eli5: A joint should only talk to neighbors it already knows. Otherwise a stranger could plug your pipe into the wrong place.
